ety.text: From Middle English tune, an unexplained variant of tone, from Old French ton, from Latin tonus, from Ancient Greek τόνος (tónos, “a tone”). Doublet of tone, ton, and tonus.

senses.d: A melody.
ex: Eric played a catchy tune on his acoustic guitar and Alyssa played the drums.

senses.d: A song, or short musical composition.
The act of tuning or maintenance.
ex: Your engine needs a good tune.

senses.d: The state or condition of being correctly tuned.
ex: Your engine is now in tune.
This piano is not in tune.

senses.d: Temper; frame of mind.
A sound; a note; a tone.
ex: Pray you now, if it may the ſtand with the tune of your voices, that I may bee Conſull, I haue heere the Cuſtomarie Gowne.

senses.d: Order; harmony; concord.
ex: A child will learn three times as much when he is in tune, as when he […] is dragged unwillingly to [his task].

senses.d: Used to show appreciation or approval of a song.
ex: You heard the new Rizzle Kicks song? — Tune!

senses.d: To adjust (a musical instrument) so that it produces the correct pitches.
ex: to tune a piano or a violin
The Harpe. […] A harper with his wreſt maye tune the harpe wrong / Mys tunying of an Inſtrument ſhal hurt a true ſonge

senses.d: To adjust or modify (especially a mechanical or electrical device) so that it functions optimally.
ex: Tuning the engine gave me an extra twenty horsepower.
Tune your mind, and anything becomes possible.

senses.d: To adjust the frequency of a transmitter or receiver, such as on a radio or TV transmitter or receiver, so as to send or receive an electromagnetic signal through a desired frequency band or channel.
ex: Tune to Channel 6 for all your favourite daytime shows.

senses.d: Of faculties, senses, etc.: to adapt to or direct towards a particular target.
ex: My ears were tuned to the sounds of the forest.

senses.d: To make more precise, intense, or effective; to put into a proper state or disposition.
ex: [H]ee hath incurred the euerlaſting diſpleaſure of the King, who had euen tun'd his bounty to ſing happineſſe to him.

senses.d: To produce a particular quality of voice by adjusting singing voice synthesis software.
ex: […] Those who are highly skilled in manipulating the Vocaloid technology—e.g., tuning Miku's singing voices—arrange existing[…]
LOLA's voice is used simply to render basic notes and words with no pitch or expression tuning applied.

senses.d: To adjust the frequency of a transmitter or receiver, such as on a radio or TV transmitter or receiver, so as to send or receive an electromagnetic signal through a desired frequency band or channel.
To attune; to adapt in style of music; to make harmonious.
ex: For now to ſorrow must I tune my ſong, / And ſet my Harpe to notes of ſaddeſt wo, […]

senses.d: To give a certain tone or character to.
To set (lyrics) to music.
ex: Ginsberg sang some poems from William Blake which he had "tuned".
